# SiPhon

**An open silicon photonics design toolkit** — material dispersion models, waveguide mode
solvers, S-parameter circuit simulation, WDM system math, closed-form optical link budgets
for AI-datacenter interconnects, and Monte Carlo corner/yield analysis.

SiPhon is the open-core engine ("Product 0") of the startup thesis developed in this repo:
the loudest unsolved bottleneck in the AI-datacenter photonics buildout is predicting,
testing, and yielding co-packaged optics — see [docs/THESIS.md](docs/THESIS.md) for the
plan and [docs/RESEARCH.md](docs/RESEARCH.md) for the 21,000-word industry deep-research
report behind it (July 2026; 28-agent research run, raw transcripts in
[docs/research/](docs/research/)).

## Install & test

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest          # 144 tests
```

## What's inside

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `siphon.materials` | Sellmeier refractive-index models (Si, SiO₂, Si₃N₄) with validity ranges, thermo-optic coefficients, material group index |
| `siphon.waveguide` | Exact three-layer slab TE/TM mode solver; effective-index-method strip/rib solver; n_eff, group index, chromatic dispersion; bend-loss heuristic |
| `siphon.components` | S-parameter models: straight, directional coupler, Y-branch, phase shifters, grating coupler, all-pass & add-drop rings (Bogaerts 2012), analytic MZI |
| `siphon.circuit` | Netlist-level S-matrix circuit solver (subnetwork reduction with proper feedback handling — rings built from couplers work) |
| `siphon.link` | IM-DD link-budget engine: Q-from-BER (NRZ/PAM4), thermal-limited sensitivity, ER/RIN/crosstalk penalties, waterfall reports, energy-per-bit breakdowns, CPO & pluggable presets |
| `siphon.wdm` | Channel plans (CWDM4/LR4/DWDM grids), ring FSR/channel-count limits, thermal-tuning power, aggregate crosstalk |
| `siphon.montecarlo` | Monte Carlo corner analysis: truncated-normal/uniform parameters, parametric yield, sensitivity ranking, ASCII distribution reports |

## Quick taste

```python
from siphon import link, waveguide

wg = waveguide.Waveguide(width_um=0.5, height_um=0.22)
print(wg.neff(1.55), wg.group_index(1.55))   # 2.49, 4.02 (EIM)

cpo = link.preset_cpo_optical_io()
print(cpo.report())                          # full dB waterfall, TX -> margin
print(cpo.margin_db)                         # +11.4 dB nominal
```

## Examples

```bash
uv run python examples/01_waveguide_explorer.py    # mode solving, single-mode limits
uv run python examples/02_ring_wdm_filter.py       # 4-channel ring demux design
uv run python examples/03_cpo_vs_pluggable.py      # flagship: two link waterfalls + pJ/bit
uv run python examples/04_monte_carlo_yield.py     # lane yield + dominant-variation ranking
```

## Scope and honesty

Everything here is closed-form or semi-analytic physics — fast, transparent, and
dependency-free, accurate to the level a system architect needs for budgeting and corner
exploration. It is **not** a substitute for full-vectorial mode solvers or FDTD for device
signoff, and the presets are published-data-plausible illustrations, not measured silicon.
The point of the open engine is exactly that gap: the proprietary layer the thesis builds
toward is calibration against measured wafer/test data.

## Repo map

```
src/siphon/          the toolkit
tests/               144 tests, physics anchored to analytic/known values
examples/            four runnable demos
docs/RESEARCH.md     industry deep-research report (July 2026)
docs/THESIS.md       ranked startup theses + recommended play
docs/research/       full raw evidence: agent transcripts, judge verdicts, sources
```

309	class RingAllPass:
310	    """All-pass (notch) ring resonator, single bus.
311	
312	    through = (t - a e^{i phi}) / (1 - t a e^{i phi})  [Bogaerts 2012, Eq. 2]
313	    with self-coupling t = sqrt(1 - kappa_power), round-trip amplitude
314	    a = 10**(-loss_db_per_cm * circumference_um * 1e-4 / 20), and round-trip
315	    phase phi = 2*pi * n_eff(wl) * circumference_um / wl (linearized n_eff).
316	    Critical coupling (a == t) gives full extinction at resonance.
317	
318	    Parameters
319	    ----------
320	    circumference_um : ring round-trip length in um.
321	    neff0, ng : effective and group index at wl0_um.
322	    kappa_power : bus-ring power coupling in [0, 1].
323	    loss_db_per_cm : round-trip propagation loss in dB/cm.
324	    wl0_um : dispersion expansion wavelength in um.
325	    """
326	
327	    circumference_um: float
328	    neff0: float
329	    ng: float
330	    kappa_power: float = 0.1
331	    loss_db_per_cm: float = 0.0
332	    wl0_um: float = 1.55
333	
334	    ports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("in", "out")
335	
336	    def __post_init__(self):
337	        if self.circumference_um <= 0:
338	            raise ValueError("circumference_um must be positive")
339	        _check_coupling("kappa_power", self.kappa_power)
340	
341	    def _round_trip(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:
342	        a = _amp_from_db(self.loss_db_per_cm * self.circumference_um * 1e-4)
343	        neff = _linear_neff(wl, self.neff0, self.ng, self.wl0_um)
344	        phi = 2.0 * np.pi * neff * self.circumference_um / wl
345	        return a, phi

347	    def s_params(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
348	        wl = _wl_array(wl)
349	        a, phi = self._round_trip(wl)
350	        t = np.sqrt(1.0 - self.kappa_power)
351	        ae = a * np.exp(1j * phi)
352	        return _two_port((t - ae) / (1.0 - t * ae))

355	@dataclass
356	class RingAddDrop:
357	    """Add-drop ring resonator with two bus waveguides.
358	
359	    Analytic transfer functions per Bogaerts et al., Laser Photon. Rev. 6,
360	    47 (2012), Eqs. 4-5, with self-couplings t_i = sqrt(1 - kappa_i),
361	    round-trip amplitude a and phase phi as in :class:`RingAllPass`
362	    (D = 1 - t1 t2 a e^{i phi}):
363	
364	        in -> through :  (t1 - t2 a e^{i phi}) / D
365	        in -> drop    :  -sqrt(kappa1 kappa2) sqrt(a) e^{i phi/2} / D
366	        add -> drop   :  (t2 - t1 a e^{i phi}) / D
367	        add -> through:  same as in -> drop (device symmetry)
368	
369	    The drop path traverses half the ring (sqrt(a) e^{i phi/2}); couplers
370	    are assumed point-like and lossless. in<->add and through<->drop carry
371	    counter-propagating signals with no direct coupling, so those S entries
372	    are 0, as are all reflections. The 4x4 is reciprocal, and unitary when
373	    loss_db_per_cm == 0.
374	
375	    Parameters
376	    ----------
377	    circumference_um : ring round-trip length in um.
378	    neff0, ng : effective and group index at wl0_um.
379	    kappa1_power, kappa2_power : input/drop bus power couplings in [0, 1].
380	    loss_db_per_cm : round-trip propagation loss in dB/cm.
381	    wl0_um : dispersion expansion wavelength in um.
382	    """
383	
384	    circumference_um: float
385	    neff0: float
386	    ng: float
387	    kappa1_power: float = 0.1
388	    kappa2_power: float = 0.1
389	    loss_db_per_cm: float = 0.0
390	    wl0_um: float = 1.55
391	
392	    ports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("in", "through", "add", "drop")
393	
394	    def __post_init__(self):
395	        if self.circumference_um <= 0:
396	            raise ValueError("circumference_um must be positive")
397	        _check_coupling("kappa1_power", self.kappa1_power)
398	        _check_coupling("kappa2_power", self.kappa2_power)
399	
400	    def s_params(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
401	        wl = _wl_array(wl)
402	        a = _amp_from_db(self.loss_db_per_cm * self.circumference_um * 1e-4)
403	        neff = _linear_neff(wl, self.neff0, self.ng, self.wl0_um)
404	        phi = 2.0 * np.pi * neff * self.circumference_um / wl
405	        t1 = np.sqrt(1.0 - self.kappa1_power)
406	        t2 = np.sqrt(1.0 - self.kappa2_power)
407	        ae = a * np.exp(1j * phi)
408	        half = np.sqrt(a) * np.exp(1j * phi / 2.0)
409	        denom = 1.0 - t1 * t2 * ae
410	
411	        thru = (t1 - t2 * ae) / denom
412	        drop = -np.sqrt(self.kappa1_power * self.kappa2_power) * half / denom
413	        add_thru = (t2 - t1 * ae) / denom
414	
415	        s = np.zeros((wl.size, 4, 4), dtype=complex)
416	        s[:, 1, 0] = s[:, 0, 1] = thru  # in <-> through
417	        s[:, 3, 0] = s[:, 0, 3] = drop  # in <-> drop
418	        s[:, 2, 1] = s[:, 1, 2] = drop  # add <-> through
419	        s[:, 3, 2] = s[:, 2, 3] = add_thru  # add <-> drop
420	        return s

427	class MZI:
428	    """Unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer, composed analytically.
429	
430	    Forward transfer matrix M = C_out @ diag(arm phases) @ C_in, where the
431	    C's are :class:`DirectionalCoupler` 2x2 transfer blocks and the arms
432	    carry exp(-1j * 2*pi * n_eff(wl) * L / wl) with lengths (dl_um, 0):
433	    only the differential path is modeled; common arm length adds a global
434	    phase and loss omitted here. Propagation loss (loss_db_per_cm) therefore
435	    acts on the dl_um arm only. Port mapping matches
436	    :class:`DirectionalCoupler`: in0 -> out0 is the bar path.
437	
438	    With 50/50 couplers: |bar|^2 = sin^2(dphi/2), |cross|^2 = cos^2(dphi/2)
439	    with dphi = 2*pi*n_eff(wl)*dl/wl; FSR ~= wl^2/(ng*dl).
440	
441	    Parameters
442	    ----------
443	    dl_um : arm length imbalance in um.
444	    neff0, ng : arm effective and group index at wl0_um.
445	    coupling_in, coupling_out : splitter/combiner power couplings in [0, 1].
446	    loss_db_per_cm : arm propagation loss in dB/cm (differential arm only).
447	    wl0_um : dispersion expansion wavelength in um.
448	    """
449	
450	    dl_um: float
451	    neff0: float
452	    ng: float
453	    coupling_in: float = 0.5
454	    coupling_out: float = 0.5
455	    loss_db_per_cm: float = 0.0
456	    wl0_um: float = 1.55

458	    ports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("in0", "in1", "out0", "out1")

461	        if self.dl_um < 0:
462	            raise ValueError("dl_um must be non-negative")
463	        _check_coupling("coupling_in", self.coupling_in)
464	        _check_coupling("coupling_out", self.coupling_out)
465	
466	    def s_params(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
467	        wl = _wl_array(wl)
468	        c_in = DirectionalCoupler(self.coupling_in)._transfer()
469	        c_out = DirectionalCoupler(self.coupling_out)._transfer()
470	
471	        arm = Straight(
472	            self.dl_um, self.neff0, self.ng, self.loss_db_per_cm, self.wl0_um
473	        ).s_params(wl)[:, 1, 0]
474	        phases = np.zeros((wl.size, 2, 2), dtype=complex)
475	        phases[:, 0, 0] = arm  # differential arm, length dl_um
476	        phases[:, 1, 1] = 1.0  # reference arm, length 0
477	
478	        m = c_out @ phases @ c_in  # (n, 2, 2) forward transfer
479	        s = np.zeros((wl.size, 4, 4), dtype=complex)
480	        s[:, 2:, :2] = m
481	        s[:, :2, 2:] = np.swapaxes(m, 1, 2)
482	        return s

1	"""Frequency-domain S-parameter circuit solver.
2	
3	Assembles a netlist of S-parameter models into a single external S-matrix by
4	eliminating internal (connected) ports, the standard multiport interconnection
5	method (Filipsson 1981; also known as subnetwork growth). Per wavelength the
6	block-diagonal S of all instances is partitioned into external (e) and
7	internal (i) ports; with P the permutation exchanging each connected pair
8	(a_i = P b_i),
9	
10	    S_ext = S_ee + S_ei P (I - S_ii P)^-1 S_ie.
11	
12	Model protocol: a model exposes ``ports: tuple[str, ...]`` and
13	``s_params(wl) -> ndarray`` of shape ``(len(wl), n, n)``, complex, with
14	b_p = sum_q S[k, p, q] a_q at vacuum wavelength ``wl[k]`` in um. Port order in
15	the matrix equals the order of ``ports``.
16	
17	Validity: linear, time-invariant, single-mode-per-port networks only. A
18	lossless feedback loop exactly on resonance makes (I - S_ii P) singular — the
19	physical steady state does not exist — and raises rather than returning noise.
20	
21	Conventions: wavelengths in um; ``transmission_db`` returns power dB.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import numpy as np
27	
28	# Condition number of (I - S_ii P) above which the internal solve is treated
29	# as singular (resonant lossless loop, or a model with gain >= loop loss).
30	_COND_LIMIT = 1e12
31	
32	Port = tuple[str, str]  # (instance name, port name)
33	
34	
35	class Circuit:
36	    """Netlist of S-parameter model instances solved to one external S-matrix.
37	
38	    Build with :meth:`add`, wire with :meth:`connect`, name outside-world
39	    ports with :meth:`expose`, then call :meth:`s_params`. External port
40	    order in the result is the order of the ``expose`` calls.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(self) -> None:
44	        self._instances: dict[str, object] = {}
45	        self._connections: list[tuple[Port, Port]] = []
46	        self._exposed: dict[str, Port] = {}
47	        self._used_ports: set[Port] = set()
48	
49	    # --- construction ------------------------------------------------------
50	
51	    def add(self, name: str, model) -> None:
52	        """Register a model instance under a unique name."""
53	        if name in self._instances:
54	            raise ValueError(f"instance {name!r} already added")
55	        ports = getattr(model, "ports", None)
56	        if not ports or not hasattr(model, "s_params"):
57	            raise TypeError(
58	                f"model for {name!r} must expose 'ports' and 's_params(wl)'"
59	            )
60	        if len(set(ports)) != len(ports):
61	            raise ValueError(f"model for {name!r} has duplicate port names: {ports}")
62	        self._instances[name] = model
63	
64	    def connect(self, a: Port, b: Port) -> None:
65	        """Join two instance ports. Each port may be used at most once."""
66	        self._resolve(a)
67	        self._resolve(b)
68	        if a == b:
69	            raise ValueError(f"cannot connect port {a} to itself")
70	        for port in (a, b):
71	            if port in self._used_ports:
72	                raise ValueError(f"port {port} is already connected or exposed")
73	        self._connections.append((a, b))
74	        self._used_ports.update((a, b))
75	
76	    def expose(self, external_name: str, port: Port) -> None:
77	        """Make an instance port an external port named ``external_name``."""
78	        self._resolve(port)
79	        if external_name in self._exposed:
80	            raise ValueError(f"external port {external_name!r} already defined")
81	        if port in self._used_ports:
82	            raise ValueError(f"port {port} is already connected or exposed")
83	        self._exposed[external_name] = port
84	        self._used_ports.add(port)
85	
86	    @property
87	    def external_ports(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
88	        """External port names in expose() order (== S-matrix port order)."""
89	        return tuple(self._exposed)
90	
91	    def _resolve(self, port: Port) -> int:
92	        """Global port index of (instance, port); raises if unknown."""
93	        inst, pname = port
94	        if inst not in self._instances:
95	            raise KeyError(f"unknown instance {inst!r}; known: {sorted(self._instances)}")
96	        offset = 0
97	        for name, model in self._instances.items():
98	            if name == inst:
99	                break
100	            offset += len(model.ports)
101	        model = self._instances[inst]
102	        if pname not in model.ports:
103	            raise KeyError(
104	                f"instance {inst!r} has no port {pname!r}; ports: {model.ports}"
105	            )
106	        return offset + model.ports.index(pname)
107	
108	    # --- solve --------------------------------------------------------------
109	
110	    def s_params(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
111	        """External S-matrix, shape (len(wl), n_ext, n_ext), wl in um.
112	
113	        Raises ValueError if any instance port is neither connected nor
114	        exposed, and numpy.linalg.LinAlgError if the internal solve is
115	        singular at some wavelength (lossless resonant loop).
116	        """
117	        wl = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(wl, dtype=float))
118	        if not self._instances:
119	            raise ValueError("circuit has no instances")
120	
121	        dangling = [
122	            (name, pname)
123	            for name, model in self._instances.items()
124	            for pname in model.ports
125	            if (name, pname) not in self._used_ports
126	        ]
127	        if dangling:
128	            raise ValueError(f"unconnected and unexposed ports: {dangling}")
129	
130	        n_total = sum(len(m.ports) for m in self._instances.values())
131	        s_block = np.zeros((len(wl), n_total, n_total), dtype=complex)
132	        offset = 0
133	        for name, model in self._instances.items():
134	            n = len(model.ports)
135	            sm = np.asarray(model.s_params(wl), dtype=complex)
136	            if sm.shape != (len(wl), n, n):
137	                raise ValueError(
138	                    f"instance {name!r}: s_params returned shape {sm.shape}, "
139	                    f"expected {(len(wl), n, n)}"
140	                )
141	            s_block[:, offset : offset + n, offset : offset + n] = sm
142	            offset += n
143	
144	        ext = np.array([self._resolve(p) for p in self._exposed.values()], dtype=int)
145	        internal_ports = [p for pair in self._connections for p in pair]
146	        internal = np.array([self._resolve(p) for p in internal_ports], dtype=int)
147	        n_i = len(internal)
148	
149	        # a_int = P b_int: each connected pair exchanges its waves.
150	        perm = np.zeros((n_i, n_i))
151	        for m in range(0, n_i, 2):
152	            perm[m, m + 1] = perm[m + 1, m] = 1.0
153	
154	        out = np.empty((len(wl), len(ext), len(ext)), dtype=complex)
155	        eye = np.eye(n_i)
156	        for k in range(len(wl)):
157	            s_ee = s_block[k][np.ix_(ext, ext)]
158	            if n_i == 0:
159	                out[k] = s_ee
160	                continue
161	            s_ei = s_block[k][np.ix_(ext, internal)]
162	            s_ie = s_block[k][np.ix_(internal, ext)]
163	            s_ii = s_block[k][np.ix_(internal, internal)]
164	            m_int = eye - s_ii @ perm
165	            if not np.all(np.isfinite(m_int)) or np.linalg.cond(m_int) > _COND_LIMIT:
166	                raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(
167	                    f"singular internal network at wavelength index {k} "
168	                    f"(wl = {wl[k]} um): lossless resonant loop or gain"
169	                )
170	            out[k] = s_ee + s_ei @ perm @ np.linalg.solve(m_int, s_ie)
171	        return out
172	
173	    # --- convenience ---------------------------------------------------------
174	
175	    def transmission(self, wl: np.ndarray, inport: str, outport: str) -> np.ndarray:
176	        """Complex field transmission b_out / a_in vs wavelength (um)."""
177	        for name in (inport, outport):
178	            if name not in self._exposed:
179	                raise KeyError(
180	                    f"unknown external port {name!r}; known: {self.external_ports}"
181	                )
182	        names = self.external_ports
183	        s = self.s_params(wl)
184	        return s[:, names.index(outport), names.index(inport)]
185

1	"""Waveguide mode solvers.
2	
3	Two levels of model, both fast and dependency-free:
4	
5	1. ``slab_neffs`` — exact transcendental solution of the three-layer slab
6	   waveguide (TE and TM), the workhorse of quick photonic reasoning.
7	2. ``Waveguide`` — strip/rib waveguide solved with the effective index
8	   method (EIM): vertical slab first, then the horizontal problem with the
9	   swapped polarization. Accurate to roughly the percent level for n_eff of
10	   well-guided modes; use a full vectorial solver for final signoff.
11	
12	Conventions: wavelengths and dimensions in um; quasi-TE means dominant
13	E-field parallel to the wafer plane.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
19	from functools import lru_cache
20	
21	import numpy as np
22	from scipy.optimize import brentq
23	
24	from . import materials

26	
27	def _slab_dispersion(neff, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness, m, polarization):
28	    """Zero of this function <=> guided slab mode m at n_eff = neff."""
29	    kappa = k0 * np.sqrt(n_core**2 - neff**2)
30	    gamma = k0 * np.sqrt(max(neff**2 - n_top**2, 0.0))
31	    delta = k0 * np.sqrt(max(neff**2 - n_bot**2, 0.0))
32	    if polarization == "TE":
33	        phi_top = np.arctan2(gamma, kappa)
34	        phi_bot = np.arctan2(delta, kappa)
35	    elif polarization == "TM":
36	        phi_top = np.arctan2((n_core / n_top) ** 2 * gamma, kappa)
37	        phi_bot = np.arctan2((n_core / n_bot) ** 2 * delta, kappa)
38	    else:
39	        raise ValueError("polarization must be 'TE' or 'TM'")
40	    return kappa * thickness - phi_top - phi_bot - m * np.pi
41	
42	
43	def slab_neffs(
44	    n_core: float,
45	    n_top: float,
46	    n_bot: float,
47	    thickness_um: float,
48	    wavelength_um: float,
49	    polarization: str = "TE",
50	    max_modes: int = 16,
51	) -> list[float]:
52	    """Effective indices of all guided modes of a three-layer slab.
53	
54	    Returns a list sorted from fundamental (highest n_eff) down; empty list
55	    if the slab guides no mode at this wavelength/polarization.
56	    """
57	    if thickness_um <= 0:
58	        return []
59	    if n_core <= max(n_top, n_bot):
60	        return []
61	    k0 = 2.0 * np.pi / wavelength_um
62	    n_min = max(n_top, n_bot)
63	    eps = 1e-9
64	    lo, hi = n_min + eps, n_core - eps
65	    out: list[float] = []
66	    for m in range(max_modes):
67	        f_lo = _slab_dispersion(lo, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization)
68	        f_hi = _slab_dispersion(hi, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization)
69	        if f_lo <= 0.0:
70	            break  # this and all higher-order modes are cut off
71	        if f_hi >= 0.0:  # numerically degenerate bracket; shouldn't happen
72	            break
73	        neff = brentq(
74	            _slab_dispersion,
75	            lo,
76	            hi,
77	            args=(k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization),
78	            xtol=1e-12,
79	        )
80	        out.append(float(neff))
81	    return out
82

84	@dataclass(frozen=True)
85	class Waveguide:
86	    """Strip or rib waveguide on SOI (or SiN) solved by the effective index method.
87	
88	    Parameters
89	    ----------
90	    width_um, height_um : core cross-section.
91	    slab_um : residual slab thickness for a rib; 0 for a fully etched strip.
92	    core, cladding, box : material names understood by :mod:`siphon.materials`.
93	        ``cladding`` is the top/side cladding, ``box`` the buried oxide.
94	    """
95	
96	    width_um: float
97	    height_um: float
98	    slab_um: float = 0.0
99	    core: str = "si"
100	    cladding: str = "sio2"
101	    box: str = "sio2"
102	
103	    def __post_init__(self):
104	        if self.width_um <= 0 or self.height_um <= 0:
105	            raise ValueError("width_um and height_um must be positive")
106	        if not 0 <= self.slab_um < self.height_um:
107	            raise ValueError("slab_um must satisfy 0 <= slab_um < height_um")
108	
109	    # --- effective index -------------------------------------------------
110	
111	    def neff(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE") -> float:
112	        """Effective index of the fundamental quasi-TE or quasi-TM mode.
113	
114	        Raises ValueError if the structure guides no such mode.
115	        """
116	        return self._neff_cached(round(float(wavelength_um), 9), mode)
117	
118	    @lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
119	    def _neff_cached(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str) -> float:
120	        n_core = materials.index(self.core, wavelength_um)
121	        n_clad = materials.index(self.cladding, wavelength_um)
122	        n_box = materials.index(self.box, wavelength_um)
123	
124	        # EIM polarization bookkeeping: quasi-TE of the channel guide uses the
125	        # TE slab solution vertically, then TM horizontally (and vice versa).
126	        vert_pol = "TE" if mode.upper() == "TE" else "TM"
127	        horiz_pol = "TM" if mode.upper() == "TE" else "TE"
128	
129	        core_slab = slab_neffs(n_core, n_clad, n_box, self.height_um, wavelength_um, vert_pol)
130	        if not core_slab:
131	            raise ValueError(
132	                f"no vertical slab mode for {self!r} at {wavelength_um} um ({mode})"
133	            )
134	        n_center = core_slab[0]
135	
136	        if self.slab_um > 0:
137	            side_slab = slab_neffs(
138	                n_core, n_clad, n_box, self.slab_um, wavelength_um, vert_pol
139	            )
140	            n_side = side_slab[0] if side_slab else max(n_clad, n_box)
141	        else:
142	            n_side = n_clad
143	
144	        if n_center <= n_side:
145	            raise ValueError(f"no lateral confinement for {self!r} ({mode})")
146	        horiz = slab_neffs(n_center, n_side, n_side, self.width_um, wavelength_um, horiz_pol)
147	        if not horiz:
148	            raise ValueError(f"no guided mode for {self!r} at {wavelength_um} um ({mode})")
149	        return horiz[0]
150	
151	    # --- dispersion ------------------------------------------------------
152	
153	    def group_index(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE", dwl_um: float = 1e-4) -> float:
154	        """Group index n_g = n_eff - lambda d(n_eff)/d(lambda).
155	
156	        Includes both waveguide and material dispersion (materials are
157	        re-evaluated at each finite-difference point).
158	        """
159	        n0 = self.neff(wavelength_um, mode)
160	        n_p = self.neff(wavelength_um + dwl_um, mode)
161	        n_m = self.neff(wavelength_um - dwl_um, mode)
162	        dn_dwl = (n_p - n_m) / (2.0 * dwl_um)
163	        return float(n0 - wavelength_um * dn_dwl)
164	
165	    def dispersion_ps_nm_km(
166	        self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE", dwl_um: float = 5e-4
167	    ) -> float:
168	        """Chromatic dispersion parameter D = -(lambda/c) d^2 n_eff / d lambda^2.
169	
170	        Returned in the conventional units of ps/(nm*km).
171	        """
172	        n_p = self.neff(wavelength_um + dwl_um, mode)
173	        n_0 = self.neff(wavelength_um, mode)
174	        n_m = self.neff(wavelength_um - dwl_um, mode)
175	        d2n = (n_p - 2.0 * n_0 + n_m) / dwl_um**2  # 1/um^2
176	        c_um_per_ps = 2.99792458e2  # speed of light in um/ps
177	        d_ps_per_um2 = -(wavelength_um / c_um_per_ps) * d2n  # ps/um^2
178	        # convert ps per (um of bandwidth) per (um of length) -> ps/(nm*km)
179	        return float(d_ps_per_um2 * 1e-3 * 1e9)
180	
181	
182	def bend_loss_db_per_90deg(radius_um: float) -> float:
183	    """HEURISTIC pure-bend loss per 90-degree turn for a 220 nm strip Si waveguide.
184	
185	    Exponential fit anchored to published measurements (Vlasov & McNab 2004:
186	    ~0.086 dB at R=1 um, ~0.013 dB at R=2 um). Order-of-magnitude guidance
187	    only; real bend loss depends strongly on geometry, wavelength, and
188	    sidewall roughness.
189	    """
190	    if radius_um <= 0:
191	        raise ValueError("radius must be positive")
192	    a, b = 0.57, 1.89  # loss = a * exp(-b * R[um]) dB per 90 degrees
193	    return a * np.exp(-b * radius_um)

1	"""Refractive index models for common silicon-photonics materials.
2	
3	All models take vacuum wavelength in micrometers (um) and return the real
4	refractive index. Valid ranges are noted per model; outside them a ValueError
5	is raised rather than silently extrapolating.
6	
7	Thermo-optic coefficients (dn/dT, 1/K, near 1.55 um and room temperature) are
8	provided as module constants.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import numpy as np
14	
15	# Thermo-optic coefficients near 1550 nm, 300 K (1/K)
16	DN_DT_SI = 1.86e-4
17	DN_DT_SIO2 = 0.95e-5
18	DN_DT_SIN = 2.45e-5
19	
20	
21	def _as_array(wavelength_um) -> np.ndarray:
22	    wl = np.asarray(wavelength_um, dtype=float)
23	    if np.any(wl <= 0):
24	        raise ValueError("wavelength must be positive (in um)")
25	    return wl
26	
27	
28	def _check_range(wl: np.ndarray, lo: float, hi: float, name: str) -> None:
29	    if np.any(wl < lo) or np.any(wl > hi):
30	        raise ValueError(
31	            f"{name} model valid for {lo}-{hi} um; got wavelength outside range"
32	        )
33	
34	
35	def n_si(wavelength_um):
36	    """Refractive index of crystalline silicon (Li 1980 fit, 1.2-14 um).
37	
38	    n(1.55 um) ~= 3.476.
39	    """
40	    wl = _as_array(wavelength_um)
41	    _check_range(wl, 1.2, 14.0, "Si")
42	    wl2 = wl**2
43	    n2 = 11.6858 + 0.939816 / wl2 + 8.10461e-3 * wl2 / (wl2 - 1.1071**2)
44	    return np.sqrt(n2) if np.ndim(wavelength_um) else float(np.sqrt(n2))
45	
46	
47	def n_sio2(wavelength_um):
48	    """Refractive index of fused silica (Malitson 1965, 0.21-6.7 um).
49	
50	    n(1.55 um) ~= 1.444.
51	    """
52	    wl = _as_array(wavelength_um)
53	    _check_range(wl, 0.21, 6.7, "SiO2")
54	    wl2 = wl**2
55	    n2 = (
56	        1.0
57	        + 0.6961663 * wl2 / (wl2 - 0.0684043**2)
58	        + 0.4079426 * wl2 / (wl2 - 0.1162414**2)
59	        + 0.8974794 * wl2 / (wl2 - 9.896161**2)
60	    )
61	    return np.sqrt(n2) if np.ndim(wavelength_um) else float(np.sqrt(n2))
62	
63	
64	def n_sin(wavelength_um):
65	    """Refractive index of LPCVD stoichiometric Si3N4 (Luke 2015, 0.31-5.5 um).
66	
67	    n(1.55 um) ~= 1.996.
68	    """
69	    wl = _as_array(wavelength_um)
70	    _check_range(wl, 0.31, 5.5, "Si3N4")
71	    wl2 = wl**2
72	    n2 = (
73	        1.0
74	        + 3.0249 * wl2 / (wl2 - 0.1353406**2)
75	        + 40314.0 * wl2 / (wl2 - 1239.842**2)
76	    )
77	    return np.sqrt(n2) if np.ndim(wavelength_um) else float(np.sqrt(n2))
78	
79	
80	MATERIALS = {
81	    "si": n_si,
82	    "sio2": n_sio2,
83	    "sin": n_sin,
84	}

87	def index(material: str, wavelength_um):
88	    """Look up refractive index by material name ('si', 'sio2', 'sin')."""
89	    key = material.lower()
90	    if key not in MATERIALS:
91	        raise KeyError(f"unknown material {material!r}; known: {sorted(MATERIALS)}")
92	    return MATERIALS[key](wavelength_um)

95	def group_index_material(material: str, wavelength_um: float, dwl_um: float = 1e-4) -> float:
96	    """Material group index n_g = n - lambda * dn/dlambda (central difference)."""
97	    n = index(material, wavelength_um)
98	    dn = (index(material, wavelength_um + dwl_um) - index(material, wavelength_um - dwl_um)) / (
99	        2.0 * dwl_um
100	    )
101	    return float(n - wavelength_um * dn)

2	
3	Channel plans, ring-bank capacity limits, thermal tuning power estimates,
4	and worst-case crosstalk aggregation. All wavelengths in um unless a name
5	says otherwise (``*_nm``); frequencies in GHz/THz as named; power in mW;
6	isolation/crosstalk in dB.

8	Frequency <-> wavelength conversion uses f[GHz] = C_UM_GHZ / wl[um] with
9	C_UM_GHZ = 2.99792458e5 um*GHz (vacuum speed of light).

19	# Speed of light expressed so that f[GHz] * wl[um] = C_UM_GHZ.

24	# integrated (doped-Si or metal) heater: ~0.25 nm of resonance shift per mW

122	    (heat) a silicon ring, so a blue-shift request is assumed to be realized
123	    by tuning the long way to the next resonance order at the same |detune|
124	    cost — i.e. this uses the magnitude of the detuning.

143	    that the target is redefined to the nearest order red of the resonance,

156	
157	    d(lambda)/dT = lambda * (dn_eff/dT) / n_g (from the resonance condition
158	    n_eff L = m lambda, including first-order dispersion via n_g).
159	
160	    The default dn_eff/dT scales the silicon material thermo-optic
161	    coefficient (1.86e-4 /K, :data:`siphon.materials.DN_DT_SI`) by a typical

164	    n_g = 4.2 this gives ~0.058 nm/K (~58 pm/K), consistent with measured

173	    """Worst-case aggregate crosstalk (dB, negative) from ``n_aggressors``.
174	
175	    Incoherent power sum of ``n_aggressors`` equal-power aggressors each
176	    suppressed by ``per_channel_isolation_db`` (positive dB of isolation):
177	    XT = 10 log10(n * 10^(-iso/10)). Worst case in the sense that every
178	    aggressor is assumed at full power at the victim's worst filter
179	    rejection; coherent beating penalties are not included.
180	    """
181	    if per_channel_isolation_db < 0:
182	        raise ValueError("per_channel_isolation_db must be non-negative (dB of isolation)")
183	    if n_aggressors < 1:
184	        raise ValueError("n_aggressors must be >= 1")
185	    return 10.0 * np.log10(n_aggressors * 10.0 ** (-per_channel_isolation_db / 10.0))

188	def laser_grid_check(plan: ChannelPlan, ring_fsr_nm: float) -> None:
189	    """Check that a channel plan fits within one ring FSR.
190	
191	    Raises ValueError if the plan's wavelength span exceeds ``ring_fsr_nm``
192	    (edge channels would alias onto adjacent resonance orders); emits a
193	    UserWarning if the span exceeds 90% of the FSR, leaving little guard
194	    band for thermal drift and fabrication offset.
195	    """
196	    if ring_fsr_nm <= 0:

200	        raise ValueError(
201	            f"channel span {span:.2f} nm exceeds ring FSR {ring_fsr_nm:.2f} nm; "
202	            "edge channels alias onto adjacent resonance orders"
203	        )
204	    if span > 0.9 * ring_fsr_nm:
205	        warnings.warn(
206	            f"channel span {span:.2f} nm uses >90% of ring FSR {ring_fsr_nm:.2f} nm; "
207	            "little guard band remains for drift",
208	            UserWarning,
209	            stacklevel=2,
210	        )

1	"""Optical link-budget engine for IM-DD datacom interconnects.
2	
3	Closed-form power and energy budgets for intensity-modulated direct-detect
4	links (NRZ and PAM-M), the arithmetic a co-packaged-optics system architect
5	runs before anyone opens a circuit simulator.
6	
7	Conventions
8	-----------
9	* Optical power in dBm (mW where named), losses/penalties in dB, symbol
10	  rates in GBd, energies in fJ/bit or pJ/bit as named.
11	* Modulation amplitude is tracked as *outer* OMA (optical modulation
12	  amplitude, P_top - P_bottom); receiver sensitivity is likewise an OMA.
13	* The receiver is thermal-noise-limited: the TIA input-referred current
14	  noise dominates. Shot noise, dark current, and ISI are neglected;
15	  RIN, finite extinction ratio, and crosstalk are layered on as separate
16	  dB penalties, following standard budgeting practice (Agrawal,
17	  *Fiber-Optic Communication Systems*, 4th ed., ch. 4; IEEE 802.3
18	  link-budget spreadsheets).
19	
20	Validity: architecture-level numbers, not compliance signoff. There is no
21	TDECQ machinery and no bandwidth/equalization modeling; equalization and
22	ISI effects must be entered as explicit penalties.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import math
28	from dataclasses import dataclass
29	
30	from scipy.special import erfc, erfcinv
31	
32	from .constants import db_to_linear, dbm_to_mw, mw_to_dbm

34	# Noise bandwidth of an optimized baud-rate receiver, as a fraction of the
35	# symbol rate. 0.75 * baud is the conventional value for a receiver with
36	# ~0.5-0.7 * baud 3-dB bandwidth (e.g. IEEE 802.3 sensitivity math).
37	NOISE_BANDWIDTH_FRACTION = 0.75

40	# --- BER <-> Q ------------------------------------------------------------
41	
42	
43	def q_from_ber(target_ber: float, levels: int) -> float:
44	    """Per-eye Q factor required for a target pre-FEC BER with PAM-M.
45	
46	    Uses the equal-eye PAM-M symbol error rate SER = 2 (1 - 1/M) Q(q),
47	    Q(x) = erfc(x / sqrt 2) / 2 the Gaussian tail, together with the
48	    Gray-coding approximation BER = SER / log2(M) (one bit flip per symbol
49	    error; standard and accurate at low error rates).
50	    """
51	    _check_levels(levels)
52	    if not 0.0 < target_ber < 0.5:
53	        raise ValueError("target_ber must be in (0, 0.5)")
54	    ser = target_ber * math.log2(levels)
55	    tail = ser / (2.0 * (1.0 - 1.0 / levels))
56	    if tail >= 0.5:
57	        raise ValueError("target BER is above the PAM-M random-guess floor")
58	    return float(math.sqrt(2.0) * erfcinv(2.0 * tail))
59	
60	
61	def ber_from_q(q: float, levels: int) -> float:
62	    """Pre-FEC BER of PAM-M at per-eye Q factor q (inverse of q_from_ber)."""
63	    _check_levels(levels)
64	    ser = 2.0 * (1.0 - 1.0 / levels) * 0.5 * erfc(q / math.sqrt(2.0))
65	    return float(ser / math.log2(levels))
66	
67	
68	def _check_levels(levels: int) -> None:
69	    if levels < 2 or 2 ** int(round(math.log2(levels))) != levels:
70	        raise ValueError("levels must be a power of two >= 2 (2=NRZ, 4=PAM4, ...)")

204	# --- sensitivity and penalties ---------------------------------------------
205	
206	
207	def receiver_sensitivity_oma_dbm(pd: Photodiode, tia: Tia, sig: Signaling) -> float:
208	    """Thermal-noise-limited receiver sensitivity as outer OMA, in dBm.
209	
210	    With M equally spaced levels, eye spacing OMA/(M-1), Gaussian TIA noise
211	    of rms i_n at each level and the decision thresholds mid-eye, hitting
212	    per-eye Q = q requires
213	
214	        OMA_outer = 2 q (M-1) i_n / R,      i_n = S_i sqrt(f_n),
215	
216	    with responsivity R, input noise density S_i, and noise bandwidth
217	    f_n = 0.75 * baud (see NOISE_BANDWIDTH_FRACTION). Assumes no shot
218	    noise, no signal-dependent noise, and no ISI; RIN, extinction, and
219	    crosstalk are separate penalties (see LinkBudget.sensitivity_oma_dbm).
220	    """
221	    q = sig.q_factor
222	    f_n_hz = NOISE_BANDWIDTH_FRACTION * sig.rate_gbd * 1e9
223	    i_n_a = tia.input_noise_pa_per_sqrt_hz * 1e-12 * math.sqrt(f_n_hz)
224	    oma_w = 2.0 * q * (sig.levels - 1) * i_n_a / pd.responsivity_a_per_w
225	    return float(mw_to_dbm(oma_w * 1e3))
226	
227	
228	def er_penalty_db(er_db: float) -> float:
229	    """Extinction-ratio power penalty, dB: 10 log10((ER+1)/(ER-1)).
230	
231	    The classic penalty relating average power to eye opening for finite
232	    outer extinction ratio ER (linear); 0 dB at infinite ER (Agrawal,
233	    4th ed., eq. 4.6.4). Applied on the sensitivity side of the budget as
234	    the conventional, conservative allocation for extinction-related eye
235	    closure (residual "0"-level power, threshold offset).
236	    """
237	    if er_db <= 0.0:
238	        raise ValueError("extinction ratio must be > 0 dB")
239	    if math.isinf(er_db):
240	        return 0.0
241	    er = db_to_linear(er_db)
242	    return 10.0 * math.log10((er + 1.0) / (er - 1.0))
243	
244	
245	def rin_penalty_db(rin_db_hz: float, rate_gbd: float, q: float, levels: int) -> float:
246	    """Laser RIN power penalty, dB, for a thermal-limited PAM-M receiver.
247	
248	    The top level P_top ~ OMA carries relative intensity noise of rms
249	    r = sqrt(RIN * f_n), f_n = 0.75 * baud. Requiring the top eye
250	    (spacing OMA/(M-1)) to still reach Q = q against the combined
251	    thermal + RIN noise inflates the needed OMA by
252	
253	        penalty = -5 log10(1 - (2 q r (M-1))^2)
254	
255	    (same structure as Agrawal 4th ed., eq. 4.7.3, generalized to PAM-M
256	    with the noise evaluated at the top level). Raises ValueError when
257	    2 q r (M-1) >= 1: RIN alone then makes the target BER unreachable at
258	    any power.
259	    """
260	    _check_levels(levels)
261	    f_n_hz = NOISE_BANDWIDTH_FRACTION * rate_gbd * 1e9
262	    r = math.sqrt(db_to_linear(rin_db_hz) * f_n_hz)
263	    x = 2.0 * q * r * (levels - 1)
264	    if x >= 1.0:
265	        raise ValueError(
266	            f"RIN {rin_db_hz} dB/Hz makes target unreachable at {rate_gbd} GBd "
267	            f"PAM{levels} (2*q*r*(M-1) = {x:.2f} >= 1)"
268	        )
269	    return -5.0 * math.log10(1.0 - x * x)
270	
271	
272	def crosstalk_penalty_db(agg_crosstalk_db: float) -> float:
273	    """Power penalty for aggregate in-band crosstalk, dB.
274	
275	    For total crosstalk power a fraction X (dB, negative) of the signal,
276	    the eye closes by (1 - X_linear):  penalty = -10 log10(1 - 10^(X/10)).
277	    Coherent-beat enhancement is not modeled; treat as a floor.
278	    """
279	    if agg_crosstalk_db >= 0.0:
280	        raise ValueError("aggregate crosstalk must be < 0 dB")
281	    return -10.0 * math.log10(1.0 - db_to_linear(agg_crosstalk_db))
282

295	@dataclass
296	class LinkBudget:
297	    """End-to-end IM-DD link budget in the OMA domain.
298	
299	    Composition (all dB):
300	
301	        launched OMA  = laser power - modulator IL - modulation loss
302	                        + 10 log10(2 (ER-1)/(ER+1))   [avg -> outer OMA]
303	        received OMA  = launched OMA - sum(path losses)
304	        required OMA  = thermal-limited sensitivity OMA
305	                        + ER penalty + RIN penalty + explicit penalties
306	        margin        = received OMA - required OMA
307	
308	    ``penalties_db`` holds named explicit allocations (ISI/TDECQ, MPI,
309	    crosstalk via :func:`crosstalk_penalty_db`, aging, ...).
310	    """
311	
312	    laser: Laser
313	    modulator: Modulator
314	    path: list[LossElement]
315	    photodiode: Photodiode
316	    tia: Tia
317	    signaling: Signaling
318	    penalties_db: dict[str, float] | None = None
319	
320	    # -- transmit side -----------------------------------------------------
321	
322	    @property
323	    def _avg_to_oma_db(self) -> float:
324	        """10 log10(OMA / P_avg) = 10 log10(2 (ER-1)/(ER+1)); +3.01 dB at inf ER."""
325	        er = db_to_linear(self.modulator.extinction_ratio_db)
326	        if math.isinf(er):
327	            return 10.0 * math.log10(2.0)
328	        return 10.0 * math.log10(2.0 * (er - 1.0) / (er + 1.0))
329	
330	    @property
331	    def average_launch_power_dbm(self) -> float:
332	        """Average optical power leaving the modulator, dBm."""
333	        return (
334	            self.laser.power_dbm
335	            - self.modulator.insertion_loss_db
336	            - self.modulator.modulation_loss_db
337	        )
338	
339	    @property
340	    def launched_oma_dbm(self) -> float:
341	        """ER-limited outer OMA leaving the modulator, dBm."""
342	        return self.average_launch_power_dbm + self._avg_to_oma_db
343	
344	    # -- channel -------------------------------------------------------------
345	
346	    @property
347	    def path_loss_db(self) -> float:
348	        return sum(e.loss_db for e in self.path)
349	
350	    @property
351	    def received_oma_dbm(self) -> float:
352	        """Outer OMA at the photodiode, dBm."""
353	        return self.launched_oma_dbm - self.path_loss_db
354	
355	    # -- receive side ---------------------------------------------------------
356	
357	    @property
358	    def _penalties(self) -> dict[str, float]:
359	        return dict(self.penalties_db or {})
360	
361	    @property
362	    def rin_penalty_db(self) -> float:
363	        return rin_penalty_db(
364	            self.laser.rin_db_hz,
365	            self.signaling.rate_gbd,
366	            self.signaling.q_factor,
367	            self.signaling.levels,
368	        )
369	
370	    @property
371	    def sensitivity_oma_dbm(self) -> float:
372	        """Required OMA at the receiver, dBm.
373	
374	        Thermal-limited sensitivity (:func:`receiver_sensitivity_oma_dbm`)
375	        plus, in order: ER penalty, RIN penalty, then every entry of
376	        ``penalties_db``. All penalties are independent dB add-ons — the
377	        standard (mildly pessimistic) budgeting composition.
378	        """
379	        s = receiver_sensitivity_oma_dbm(self.photodiode, self.tia, self.signaling)
380	        s += er_penalty_db(self.modulator.extinction_ratio_db)
381	        s += self.rin_penalty_db
382	        s += sum(self._penalties.values())
383	        return s
384	
385	    @property
386	    def margin_db(self) -> float:
387	        """Unallocated link margin, dB (received OMA - required OMA)."""
388	        return self.received_oma_dbm - self.sensitivity_oma_dbm
389	
390	    # -- report -----------------------------------------------------------
391	
392	    def report(self) -> str:
393	        """Aligned plain-text waterfall of the whole budget."""
394	        sig = self.signaling
395	        fmt = "PAM4" if sig.levels == 4 else ("NRZ" if sig.levels == 2 else f"PAM{sig.levels}")
396	        width = 66
397	        lines = [
398	            f"{fmt} @ {sig.rate_gbd:g} GBd ({sig.bit_rate_gbps:g} Gb/s), "
399	            f"target BER {sig.target_ber:.1e} (q = {sig.q_factor:.2f})",
400	            "-" * width,
401	        ]
402	
403	        def row(label: str, delta_db: float | None, level_dbm: float | None):
404	            d = f"{delta_db:+7.2f} dB " if delta_db is not None else " " * 11
405	            p = f"{level_dbm:+8.2f} dBm" if level_dbm is not None else ""
406	            lines.append(f"  {label:<38}{d} {p}")
407	
408	        p = self.laser.power_dbm
409	        row(f"laser line power ({self.laser.launch_reference})", None, p)
410	        p -= self.modulator.insertion_loss_db
411	        row("modulator insertion loss", -self.modulator.insertion_loss_db, p)
412	        p -= self.modulator.modulation_loss_db
413	        row("modulation loss (CW -> avg)", -self.modulator.modulation_loss_db, p)
414	        p += self._avg_to_oma_db
415	        row(
416	            f"avg -> outer OMA (ER {self.modulator.extinction_ratio_db:.1f} dB)",
417	            self._avg_to_oma_db,
418	            p,
419	        )
420	        row("launched OMA", None, p)
421	        for elem in self.path:
422	            p -= elem.loss_db
423	            row(elem.name, -elem.loss_db, p)
424	        row("received OMA", None, p)
425	        lines.append("-" * width)
426	        s = receiver_sensitivity_oma_dbm(self.photodiode, self.tia, sig)
427	        row("thermal-limited sensitivity (OMA)", None, s)
428	        d = er_penalty_db(self.modulator.extinction_ratio_db)
429	        s += d
430	        row("ER penalty", +d, s)
431	        d = self.rin_penalty_db
432	        s += d
433	        row("RIN penalty", +d, s)
434	        for name, pen in self._penalties.items():
435	            s += pen
436	            row(f"penalty: {name}", +pen, s)
437	        row("required OMA at receiver", None, s)
438	        lines.append("-" * width)
439	        m = self.margin_db
440	        lines.append(f"  {'MARGIN':<38}{'':11} {m:+8.2f} dB")
441	        return "\n".join(lines)

446	
447	def energy_per_bit_pj(
448	    link: LinkBudget,
449	    n_lanes: int,
450	    laser_shared_by: int = 1,
451	    thermal_tuning_mw_per_lane: float = 0.0,
452	    serdes_pj_per_bit: float = 4.0,
453	) -> dict[str, float]:
454	    """Electrical energy per transported bit, pJ/bit, by contributor.
455	
456	    Returns {"laser", "modulator", "tia", "tuning", "serdes", "total"},
457	    all in pJ/bit averaged over the aggregate bit rate of ``n_lanes``
458	    identical lanes (1 mW / 1 Gb/s = 1 pJ/bit).
459	
460	    * laser: one line per lane; ceil(n_lanes / laser_shared_by) lasers
461	      each emitting link.laser.power_dbm optically, converted to
462	      electrical via wall-plug efficiency (electrical = optical / wpe).
463	      ``laser_shared_by`` amortizes a shared source (split or comb line).
464	    * modulator / tia: the components' energy_fj_per_bit.
465	    * tuning: per-lane thermal tuning power (ring heaters etc.), mW.
466	    * serdes: host-side serdes/DSP allocation, pJ/bit (dominant in
467	      pluggables with full DSP; small for XSR-class CPO die-to-optics).
468	    """
469	    if n_lanes < 1 or laser_shared_by < 1:
470	        raise ValueError("n_lanes and laser_shared_by must be >= 1")
471	    lane_gbps = link.signaling.bit_rate_gbps
472	    total_gbps = n_lanes * lane_gbps
473	    n_lasers = math.ceil(n_lanes / laser_shared_by)
474	    laser_mw = n_lasers * dbm_to_mw(link.laser.power_dbm) / link.laser.wpe
475	    out = {
476	        "laser": laser_mw / total_gbps,
477	        "modulator": link.modulator.energy_fj_per_bit * 1e-3,
478	        "tia": link.tia.energy_fj_per_bit * 1e-3,
479	        "tuning": thermal_tuning_mw_per_lane / lane_gbps,
480	        "serdes": serdes_pj_per_bit,
481	    }
482	    out["total"] = sum(out.values())
483	    return out

2	
3	Photonics has no CMOS-grade statistical corner models; the practical
4	substitute is transparent Monte Carlo over declared parameter variations.
5	This module runs any scalar metric (link margin, insertion loss, Q, ...)
6	over sampled process/environment corners and reports distribution statistics
7	and parametric yield.
8	
9	Typical use::
10	
11	    params = [
12	        Normal("gc_loss_db", mean=1.75, sigma=0.25, low=0.0),
13	        Uniform("laser_power_dbm", low=11.0, high=13.0),
14	    ]
15	
16	    def margin(p):
17	        link = make_link(gc=p["gc_loss_db"], laser=p["laser_power_dbm"])
18	        return link.margin_db
19	
20	    result = run(margin, params, n=10_000, seed=1)
21	    print(result.report(threshold=0.0))
22	"""

24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
27	from dataclasses import dataclass
28	
29	import numpy as np
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class Normal:
34	    """Normally distributed parameter, optionally truncated to [low, high].
35	
36	    Truncation is by resampling, so the realized distribution is the exact
37	    truncated normal (no clipping mass at the bounds).
38	    """
39	
40	    name: str
41	    mean: float
42	    sigma: float
43	    low: float | None = None
44	    high: float | None = None
45	
46	    def __post_init__(self):
47	        if self.sigma < 0:
48	            raise ValueError("sigma must be >= 0")
49	        if self.low is not None and self.high is not None and self.low >= self.high:
50	            raise ValueError("low must be < high")
51	
52	    def sample(self, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
53	        x = rng.normal(self.mean, self.sigma, n)
54	        lo = -np.inf if self.low is None else self.low
55	        hi = np.inf if self.high is None else self.high
56	        for _ in range(1000):
57	            bad = (x < lo) | (x > hi)
58	            if not bad.any():
59	                return x
60	            x[bad] = rng.normal(self.mean, self.sigma, int(bad.sum()))
61	        raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: truncation bounds reject nearly all samples")
62	
63	
64	@dataclass(frozen=True)
65	class Uniform:
66	    """Uniformly distributed parameter on [low, high]."""
67	
68	    name: str
69	    low: float
70	    high: float
71	
72	    def __post_init__(self):
73	        if self.low >= self.high:
74	            raise ValueError("low must be < high")
75	
76	    def sample(self, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
77	        return rng.uniform(self.low, self.high, n)
78	
79	
80	Param = Normal | Uniform
81	
82	
83	@dataclass
84	class MonteCarloResult:
85	    """Samples and statistics of one scalar metric over parameter corners."""
86	
87	    metric_name: str
88	    samples: np.ndarray  # shape (n,)
89	    param_samples: dict[str, np.ndarray]
90	
91	    @property
92	    def n(self) -> int:

94	
95	    @property
96	    def n_failed(self) -> int:
97	        """Corners where the metric raised (recorded as NaN)."""
98	        return int(np.isnan(self.samples).sum())
99	
100	    @property
101	    def mean(self) -> float:
102	        return float(np.nanmean(self.samples))
103	
104	    @property
105	    def std(self) -> float:
106	        ok = self.n - self.n_failed
107	        return float(np.nanstd(self.samples, ddof=1)) if ok > 1 else 0.0
108	
109	    def percentile(self, p) -> float:
110	        return float(np.nanpercentile(self.samples, p))
111	
112	    def yield_above(self, threshold: float) -> float:
113	        """Fraction of samples with metric > threshold (parametric yield)."""
114	        return float(np.mean(self.samples > threshold))
115	
116	    def sensitivity(self) -> dict[str, float]:
117	        """Pearson correlation of each parameter with the metric.
118	
119	        A cheap screening tool: |r| near 1 means the parameter dominates the
120	        metric spread (for near-linear responses). Constant parameters get 0.
121	        """
122	        out: dict[str, float] = {}
123	        m = self.samples
124	        ms = m - m.mean()
125	        for name, x in self.param_samples.items():
126	            xs = x - x.mean()
127	            denom = np.sqrt((xs**2).sum() * (ms**2).sum())
128	            out[name] = float((xs * ms).sum() / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0
129	        return out

132	        """Plain-text distribution report with an ASCII histogram."""

138	            f"P95 {self.percentile(95):+8.3f}",

144	            )
145	        if self.n_failed:
146	            lines.append(f"  failed corners (metric raised): {self.n_failed}")
147	        counts, edges = np.histogram(self.samples[~np.isnan(self.samples)], bins=20)
148	        peak = counts.max() if counts.max() > 0 else 1
149	        lines.append("")
150	        for c, lo, hi in zip(counts, edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
151	            bar = "#" * max(0, round(width * c / peak))
152	            lines.append(f"  {lo:+9.3f} .. {hi:+9.3f} | {bar}")
153	        sens = sorted(self.sensitivity().items(), key=lambda kv: -abs(kv[1]))
154	        lines.append("")
155	        lines.append("  sensitivity (Pearson r): " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v:+.2f}" for k, v in sens))
156	        return "\n".join(lines)

158	
159	def run(
160	    metric: Callable[[dict[str, float]], float],
161	    params: Sequence[Param],
162	    n: int = 10_000,
163	    seed: int = 0,
164	    metric_name: str = "metric",
165	) -> MonteCarloResult:
166	    """Evaluate ``metric`` over ``n`` sampled corners of ``params``.
167	
168	    ``metric`` receives one dict mapping parameter name -> sampled value and
169	    returns a scalar. Sampling is reproducible for a given seed. Corners where
170	    ``metric`` raises ValueError are recorded as NaN (e.g. a corner where the
171	    RIN penalty is unreachable) and excluded from mean/std/percentiles, but a
172	    failing corner is itself yield-relevant, so NaN counts as a yield loss in
173	    :meth:`MonteCarloResult.yield_above`.
174	    """
175	    if n < 1:
176	        raise ValueError("n must be >= 1")
177	    names = [p.name for p in params]
178	    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
179	        raise ValueError("duplicate parameter names")

181	    draws = {p.name: p.sample(n, rng) for p in params}
182	    out = np.empty(n)
183	    for i in range(n):
184	        corner = {name: float(draws[name][i]) for name in names}
185	        try:
186	            out[i] = float(metric(corner))
187	        except ValueError:

findings.title: Ring models use conjugated phase convention; composing them in Circuit with other components gives wrong spectra
findings.claim: RingAllPass and RingAddDrop use exp(+1j*phi) round-trip phase while every other component (Straight, PhaseShifter, MZI) uses exp(-1j*beta*L), so the analytic ring response is the complex conjugate of the physically composed one; the module docstring's assurance that 'magnitudes, resonance positions, and linewidths are identical in either sign convention' is false as soon as a ring is placed in any multipath circuit, and Circuit silently combines the two conventions.
findings.evidence: Computed: a RingAllPass (L=100 um, kappa=0.1, 0.5 dB/cm) vs the identical ring built from DirectionalCoupler+Straight in Circuit gives t_analytic = conj(t_circuit) to 4e-12 (magnitudes equal to 2e-13, phase slope at resonance +39758 vs -39758 rad/um, i.e. group-delay sign flipped / anti-causal). Embedding each in one arm of a Circuit-built MZI with a pi/2 reference arm: analytic-ring MZI has its transmission null at 1548.98 nm, the coupler-built (physically consistent) MZI at 1549.08 nm — ~100 pm apart, with up to 45.2 dB disagreement at a fixed wavelength (-45.2 dB vs -0.05 dB). No test pins ring phase inside Circuit (tests check only magnitudes/unitarity), so this passes the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Change RingAllPass/RingAddDrop to the delay convention used everywhere else: ae = a*exp(-1j*phi) and half-ring factor sqrt(a)*exp(-1j*phi/2) (i.e. through = (t - a e^{-i phi})/(1 - t a e^{-i phi}), drop = -sqrt(k1 k2) sqrt(a) e^{-i phi/2}/D). Magnitude spectra and all existing tests are unchanged; add a regression test comparing RingAllPass phase against a DirectionalCoupler+Straight feedback loop solved by Circuit. Also correct the module-docstring claim that the sign convention cannot matter.

findings.title: LinkBudget double-counts the extinction-ratio penalty: charged in the avg->OMA conversion and again on the OMA sensitivity
findings.claim: The budget is OMA-domain: launched OMA already includes the full finite-ER reduction via _avg_to_oma_db = 10log10(2(ER-1)/(ER+1)), and the thermal-limited required OMA (2 q (M-1) i_n / R, thresholds mid-eye, level-independent noise) is ER-independent. Adding er_penalty_db(ER) = 10log10((ER+1)/(ER-1)) to sensitivity_oma_dbm charges the identical physical dB a second time; Agrawal eq. 4.6.4 applies to average-power-referenced sensitivity, and OMA-referenced budgets (the IEEE 802.3 spreadsheets the module cites) do not add it on top.
findings.evidence: Exact identity: er_penalty_db(ER) = 3.01 dB - _avg_to_oma_db(ER) for all ER (e.g. ER = 4 dB: avg->OMA = -0.65 dB, i.e. 3.66 dB below the infinite-ER +3.01 dB, and er_penalty_db = +3.66 dB — the same 3.66 dB twice). Consequence in shipped presets: preset_cpo_optical_io margin reported +11.40 dB instead of +15.06 dB physical, preset_pluggable_dr4 +6.98 dB instead of +9.82 dB — a 2.8-3.7 dB systematic error in the tool's headline output, and the README's '+11.4 dB nominal' inherits it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop er_penalty_db from sensitivity_oma_dbm and from report() (keep the function itself for users running average-power budgets, documenting that it must not be combined with an OMA-tracked launch), or equivalently track average power end-to-end and apply the ER penalty once at the receiver. Update the preset/README margins accordingly.

findings.title: MonteCarloResult.sensitivity() silently returns 0.0 for every parameter whenever any corner failed
findings.claim: sensitivity() computes Pearson r with m = self.samples without masking NaN, so a single failed corner (run() deliberately records metric ValueError as NaN, e.g. an unreachable-RIN corner) makes m.mean() and the denominator NaN; the guard 'denom > 0' is False for NaN and every parameter gets 0.0 — the advertised 'sensitivity ranking' / 'dominant-variation ranking' silently degenerates to all-zeros with no warning, and report() prints the meaningless ranking.
findings.evidence: Computed counter-example: metric(p) = 3*a + b raising ValueError when a > 2 (Normal a: mean 0 sigma 1; Uniform b: [-0.1, 0.1]), n = 2000, seed 1 -> n_failed = 52, sensitivity() = {'a': 0.0, 'b': 0.0} and report() ends with 'sensitivity (Pearson r): a +0.00, b +0.00', whereas the true correlation for a is ~ +1.0. With zero failed corners the same setup returns r_a ~ 0.999, confirming the NaN contamination is the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Mask failed corners before correlating: ok = ~np.isnan(self.samples); m = self.samples[ok]; x = x[ok] for each parameter (and return 0.0 / raise only if fewer than 2 valid samples). Add a test asserting sensitivity() still ranks parameters correctly when some corners raise.
